entry.question:
## Physical scenario

Figure shows a \( 10 \, \text{cm} \times 10 \, \text{cm} \) square bent at a \( 90^\circ \) angle. A uniform \( 0.050 \, \text{T} \) magnetic field points downward at a \( 45^\circ \) angle.

## Question

What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

## Answer choices

- A: A: \( 4.2 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{Wb} \)

- B: B: \( 3.5 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{Wb} \)

- C: C: \( 3.1 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{Wb} \)

- D: D: \( 1.6 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{Wb} \)

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image shows a bent wire loop in a three-dimensional view. The loop consists of five segments, forming a shape with dimensions indicated. The segments are labeled with lengths: the top horizontal segment is 5 cm, the vertical segment is 10 cm, and another vertical segment is 5 cm.

Blue lines with arrows represent a magnetic field (\( \vec{B} \)). The magnetic field is directed diagonally downwards to the right, forming a 45° angle with a dashed line that appears to represent a horizontal plane. The magnetic field lines are uniformly spaced and angled, highlighting the influence of the magnetic field on the loop.
